newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward cuts 400 corporate jobs.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward cuts 400 corporate jobs.

text.p: Montgomery Ward Holding Corp on Thursday said it cut 400 workers, or about 22 percent of its corporate staff, and has held talks to sell its Signature Group direct-marketing division.
The retailer said the job cuts were part of a coporate restructuring. The company would not comment how much it expected the workforce reductions to produce in savings.
Meanwhile, Montgomery Ward was negotiating the sale of its Signature division to HFS Inc, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.
The company has been negotiating with "an interested buyer," but spokeswoman Judy Gustafson would not identify the bidder. HFS declined to comment.
In a statement, Montgomery Ward Chairman and Chief Executive Roger Goddu said, "We are encouraged with the current status of the negotiations."
Montgomery Ward, the nation's 14th largest retailer, has 1,800 workers at its corporate headquarters in Chicago.
